f2_sources.finding: The lexical path walk rejects Path.is_symlink() components, then performs strict resolve, root confinement and regular-file checks. It does not test Path.is_junction().
Portable baseline is CPython >=3.12 with a Python-stdlib baseline.
WP1111 is accepted only at repository-hosted component-CI scope; runtime/physical-host/effect/completion credits remain zero.

external_sources.finding: Path.is_junction() exists since Python 3.12 and identifies Windows junctions separately from Path.is_symlink().

external_sources.version: Python 3.14.7 docs; semantics note applies to Windows name-surrogate reparse points
external_sources.finding: On Windows, stat(..., follow_symlinks=False) disables following name-surrogate reparse points including symlinks and directory junctions.
openat2 resolve restrictions exist specifically to protect userspace from race/attack scenarios involving changing path components.
RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS applies to every path component; RESOLVE_IN_ROOT confines lookup per-open and reports races/escapes fail-closed.
The legacy string-returning SecureJoin API is explicitly documented as fundamentally TOCTOU-unsafe under concurrent path mutation; newer handle-based APIs are recommended.
Linux-only handle-based safe path-resolution APIs exist, with Linux >=5.6 strongly recommended for kernel hardening.

If a future portable artifact uses tar extraction, Python 3.12 defaults remain effectively fully-trusted unless an extraction filter is explicitly selected; data filtering plus fresh temporary extraction is recommended, and live destination mutation remains outside the filter guarantee.

findings.statement: The current WP1111 lexical check is incomplete on Windows if its intended invariant is no link-like path component: CPython 3.12 distinguishes junctions from symbolic links, while F2 checks only is_symlink(). A root-internal junction can therefore plausibly survive the current lexical test and still resolve inside root.
findings.cheapest_falsifier: On Windows CPython 3.12+, create both final-component and intermediate directory junctions that target paths inside the release root and run evaluate_portable_release_static_completeness. Current code is predicted to accept the junction path unless another gate rejects it.

findings.statement: Lexical check -> resolve -> later path use is not a race-free security primitive if an attacker can mutate the release tree concurrently. Current WP1111 evidence should therefore remain a static snapshot completeness claim, not an attacker-mutable-root guarantee.
findings.cheapest_falsifier: Define the accepted threat model explicitly. If concurrent untrusted mutation is out of scope for static pre-handoff validation, no heavy path library is required here. If it is in scope, a handle-bound platform verifier is required and the current string/path pipeline must be ablated against a rename/link race.

findings.statement: No current F2 source hit was found for tar/zip extraction in the portable release path. If packaging later introduces tar extraction under the CPython 3.12 baseline, extraction must explicitly choose restrictive filtering and a fresh destination rather than relying on Python 3.12 defaults.

distillation.immediate_low_cost_candidate: Extend the lexical component check to reject Windows junctions and add Windows adversarial tests. This is stdlib-only under the existing CPython >=3.12 contract.
distillation.reason: They provide stronger Linux race-resistant primitives but add platform/dependency/license surface and are unnecessary if WP1111 remains an immutable/static release-root validator. Prefer structural distillation and only add a handle-bound hardened verifier at a later host-acceptance boundary if the threat model requires concurrent-mutation resistance.
distillation.runtime_efficiency: The junction check adds no model calls, no external dependency and negligible filesystem-check overhead; it is preferred over a framework import at equal required scope.

counterhypotheses: F2 may intentionally mean only POSIX-style symbolic-link-free rather than all Windows link-like redirects; if so, junction acceptance must be explicitly documented rather than accidentally inherited.

A Windows junction may be rejected by another current release gate before WP1111 reaches this helper; target Windows CI must test the integrated path rather than assuming the helper alone defines behavior.
Concurrent mutation may be excluded by the deterministic release-candidate construction/verification protocol; in that case TOCTOU is a threat-model boundary, not a current defect.
next_exact_action: Acquire E2_ARCHITECTURE_MAPPED create-only claim, map the junction/static-snapshot threat boundary onto WP1111 and the clean-machine acceptance path, and emit a minimal Trigger-4 candidate only if that mapping survives current-source reentry.
